static_traits.name: Li Qiongan
static_traits.social_status: Has interpersonal support (friends to talk with), but has not yet shared the negative self-feelings with friends; relationships with colleagues and friends become strained due to self-deprecation
static_traits.medical_history: Denying important physical illness; no previous psychological problem treatment or counseling experience
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, able to concretely recall key situations; neutral attitude, slightly skeptical; able to cooperate in exploration and in setting small goals; highly focused on failure experiences, prone to using absolute expressions

basic_info.main_problem: After dropping a pass in a recent football game, I concluded I am the 'worst wide receiver ever'; afterward I had intense self-criticism and inferiority, and this negative self-talk recurs and worsens after mistakes at work or in other situations.
basic_info.core_demands: Realized that these negative thoughts are affecting my self-esteem and overall well-being, and therefore seeks counseling.

special_situations.event: Dropping a crucial pass in a recent American football game
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I make a mistake at a critical moment, it equals total failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Sets excessively high expectations for themselves to avoid being seen as a failure; distracts with video games and films to temporarily relieve emotions
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am the worst wide receiver in history

special_situations.event: Getting an order wrong at work
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I make one mistake, it means my work ability is very poor
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Social withdrawal; being colder toward colleagues to reduce chances of being evaluated

special_situations.event: In the previous game, successfully caught the ball many times and scored touchdowns
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only perfect, error-free performance counts, other successes are not important
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Negates or ignores own strengths and past successes to maintain the inner standard of 'must be perfect'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: That performance does not count; this mistake is what shows the problem

special_situations.event: Placed at a critical moment, feeling everyone is counting on me
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I fail to meet expectations, I disappoint everyone, and it is all my fault
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Self-blaming and doubling demands on oneself in order to avoid disappointing others again
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I let everyone down; I am the only one to blame

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized and trusted, proving to be a capable team member at critical moments
core_conflict.fear: Afraid of disappointing others, being judged as incompetent, and being belittled
defense_goal: Gains a sense of control through self-criticism and maintaining high standards, avoiding further failure
Maintains some detachment to reduce the hurt from others' evaluations

object_relations.self_representation: A failure who disappoints people and must take full responsibility for failure
object_relations.object_representation: Others/teams who hold high expectations of me and may criticize or be disappointed

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor emphasizes her successes or offers a more balanced perspective
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Tends to think this positive evidence 'does not count', feels the counselor is downplaying her failures (regarding success as irrelevant)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Firmly uses expressions such as 'this does not mean anything / this time is not important', with a steady but firm tone, repeatedly emphasizing the difference between high standards and exceptions.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When reviewing key mistakes and the pressure of others' expectations
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believes failure is entirely borne by oneself and everyone will be disappointed because of it (excessive self-blame)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Uses highly self-blaming and absolute language (such as 'it is all my fault'), with a low tone, ignoring others or situational factors.

manifestations: When feeling low, tends to self-isolate and is colder toward colleagues and friends
Despite having friends to talk to, has not shared one's own struggles
outcomes: Strained interpersonal relationships and increased sense of alienation
Lowered self-esteem and reinforced negative self-talk

manifestations: At the start of the session, states 'part of me feels this is meaningless'
Holding a dismissive attitude toward past successes, considering them unimportant
outcomes: Substitutes distraction (video games, films) for direct coping, thereby maintaining the problem cycle

contact_model.definition: The individual ignores or avoids a stimulus from the internal or external environment, deliberately avoiding direct contact, corresponding to 'acceptance'.
manifestations: Distracting oneself with video games and movies when negative self-talk appears
When talking about success, quickly turning back to failure details to avoid contact with positive experience

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Judges oneself by the standard of 'high expectations / must be perfect'
Using absolute labels such as 'the worst' and 'complete failure' as self-measurement

exception_events.target_problem: After mistakes in key games, the client usually negates themselves catastrophically, believes they have disappointed everyone, and falls into self-criticism and low mood.
exception_events.unique_outcome: In the previous game, the client successfully caught the ball multiple times and scored touchdowns, performing stably; at that time the client did not fall into the old reaction of 'I am worthless', but made positive contributions to the team.
exception_events.reason: Clues: the client reports that at critical moments they 'usually do well', indicating stable skills and experience; the situational stress is bearable and there are past successful experiences to draw support from.

positive_force: Usually performs well under high-pressure match situations (has experience of successful catches and touchdowns)
Having social support resources such as friends (although not yet proactively shared)
Open to change (willing to try setting small goals and positive self-talk)
negative_force: Excessively high expectations and perfectionistic tendencies
Cognitive patterns such as catastrophizing, all-or-nothing thinking, negating the positive, overgeneralization, and personalization
Self-criticism leads to social avoidance and strained relationships with colleagues and friends

target_behavior.behavior: Catastrophizing self-labels and strong self-criticism (cognitive-verbal behavior)
antecedent: Key mistakes such as dropped catches occur in the game
Errors such as order mistakes occur at work
In high-pressure situations where others have expectations
target_behavior.core_reason: Internalized high expectations / perfectionism and all-or-nothing cognition, equating a single mistake with overall failure and worrying about disappointing others, tending to attribute all responsibility to themselves
target_behavior.function: Obtains a short-term sense of control and 'error-correction' through self-punishment, attempting to avoid future failure and others' negative evaluations
target_behavior.consequence: Self-esteem damaged, overall well-being declined, work performance worsened, interpersonal relationships strained, sleep and self-care affected

antecedent: Situations of interacting with colleagues or friends after experiencing a mistake
Social situations when feeling down and inferior
target_behavior.core_reason: Fears being judged and disappointing others; reduces contact due to self-negation to lower anxiety
target_behavior.function: Escaping unwelcome emotions and others' evaluations
target_behavior.consequence: Interpersonal relationships become further strained, loneliness increases, and lack of support keeps the problem cycle going

target_behavior.behavior: Coping through distraction (immersing in video games and movies)
antecedent: When negative self-talk and low mood appear
Feeling pain after repeatedly recalling failure situations
target_behavior.core_reason: Seeks short-term relief and emotion regulation, avoiding directly facing the content of self-criticism
target_behavior.function: Escapes internal discomfort and temporarily reduces the intensity of negative emotions
target_behavior.consequence: Only short-term relief; the problem and thinking patterns recur repeatedly; sleep and self-care are affected
